S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.

subtypes.Diminished Emotional Expression: A state of reduced emotional expression in facial expressions, eye contact, intonation of speech, and movements.
subtypes.Avolition: A decrease in motivated self-initiated purposeful activities.
subtypes.Alogia: A state where the quantity of spontaneous speech is significantly reduced.
subtypes.Anhedonia: A decrease in the ability to experience pleasure or interest in enjoyable activities.
subtypes.Asociality: A state where interest in social activities or interpersonal relationships is significantly reduced.

symptom.disease_info: Schizophrenia is a chronic psychotic disorder characterized by disturbances in thought, perception, and behavior, including delusions, hallucinations, disorganized thinking, and negative symptoms such as diminished motivation and emotional expression. Onset typically occurs in late adolescence or early adulthood, but later-life onset and relapses can occur, with a course that ranges from episodic to progressively deteriorating. Functional impairment in work, relationships, and self-care is common, often persisting beyond acute episodes if negative symptoms or cognitive deficits are prominent. It is differentiated from mood and substance-induced psychotic disorders by the relative independence of psychotic symptoms from mood episodes and the absence of a direct physiological cause.

patient.stressor: About two and a half years ago, Bruce took on a high-stakes consulting contract modeling water-use scenarios for a regional agency, coinciding with a major software migration at his firm and tighter-than-usual deadlines. Initially he responded by leaning into his usual habits of late-night puzzle marathons and meticulous spreadsheet checks, but colleagues noticed that his quality control reviews began taking him far longer and he increasingly resisted collaborating, insisting on redoing work that had already been signed off. Over the next two years, he became less reliable at mentoring junior analysts, missed early-morning hikes with the Trailblazers club, and started declining invitations to star-gazing meet-ups, as his preoccupation with certain project data and interpretations crowded out his previous balance of work and leisure. The situation came to a head when he repeatedly clashed with a client over what they saw as unfounded concerns in the model outputs, and his spouse, alarmed by the impact on his job and their home life, persuaded him to see a psychiatrist after his firm suggested a leave of absence.
patient.chief_complaint: “I’m here because I’m absolutely certain there are serious problems and hidden manipulations in the data at work, but no one believes me and it’s starting to cost me my job.”

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: For the last couple of years I've been completely convinced that someone—either inside the agency or higher up in government—is quietly altering the water-use data and slipping in bogus parameters, and every time I point out the patterns that prove it, people just smile, tell me it's 'within tolerance,' and treat me like I'm imagining it even though I can see the fingerprints of the manipulation all over the spreadsheets and emails.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.
S023.manifestation: These days I mostly just sit at my desk or in the living room staring at the same tables and printouts, ignoring calls from my hiking group, barely talking to my wife unless she asks me a direct question, and even then I answer in a few words because I just don't have the energy or interest to do anything—or feel much of anything—outside of chasing this one problem at work.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: In the last couple of years my work has slipped so much that my firm has taken me off projects and suggested a leave of absence, and outside of work I've pretty much stopped seeing friends or joining my hiking and star-gazing groups, which has put a real strain on my marriage and left me mostly isolated at home.
add_requirements.duration: Looking back, this whole slide—getting more withdrawn and fixated on the project and data issues—has been going on for a little over two years, ever since that big consulting contract and software change started.
add_requirements.psychotic_symptoms_duration: I've been absolutely convinced that the water-use data is being secretly tampered with for about the last couple of months, and that belief has only gotten stronger in that time.
